theoryOfChange: SAPA (Sudanese American Physicians Association) utilizes a documented approach to planning and measuring the impact of its projects, which aligns with a results framework. Their 'SAPA Project Proposal' document, available on their website, includes sections for 'Project Goals,' 'Project Objectives,' 'Expected results,' 'Deliverables,' 'Benefits,' 'Problems to be resolved,' 'Project Activities,' and 'Key Performance Indicators (KPI).' This framework details how their activities are intended to lead to specific outcomes and how these outcomes will be monitored and evaluated. Additionally, SAPA's overall strategy is described as a 'comprehensive, holistic approach to healthcare delivery' and their 'programming framework includes pillars such as Direct Health Service Delivery, Health System Resiliency, WASH, Food and Nutrition, and Protection.' A report detailing their emergency response and preparedness programming also serves as a 'framework for SAPA's programming moving forward.'

rich_narrative.summary: The Sudanese American Physicians Association (SAPA) is a medical humanitarian organization that provides critical healthcare and emergency relief to communities in Sudan and Chad. founded in 2019, the organization has transitioned from a small grassroots group to a significant medical provider. In FY2024, SAPA managed <cite id="6">$7,254,154 in total revenue</cite> to support healthcare systems and emergency services. This represents <cite id="6">early-stage growth</cite> from its FY2022 revenue of $442,259. The organization operates a direct service delivery model. This model allows them to maintain a <cite id="1">cost per beneficiary of approximately $6.96</cite>, which is exceptional for the global health sector. SAPA focuses on <cite id="4">building core health functions</cite> that can respond to crises. Their work includes <cite id="4">hunger relief, water sanitation, and empowering local physicians</cite>. The organization maintains high financial standards and is <cite id="5">verified as zakat-eligible</cite> for donors seeking to fulfill religious obligations. They hold a <cite id="1">90/100 overall score from Charity Navigator</cite>, reflecting strong accountability and leadership.
